cluster.headline: Defence ministry RFI seeks 1,000-km ship-launched loitering munition
cluster.summary: The Ministry of Defence has issued a Request for Information for a Medium Range Loitering Munition operable from ships and shore-based vehicles against maritime and land targets, requiring at least 1,000 km range and nine hours or more loiter endurance, canister-launched with a stabilised EO/IR seeker. The RFI dates from mid-August and was recirculated by trade press two days ago.

story.headline: MoD said to seek ship-launched loitering munition with 1,000-km range
story.body:
India's Ministry of Defence has issued a Request for Information for a Medium Range Loitering Munition that could be fired from ships and from shore-based vehicles against both maritime and land targets, according to trade coverage circulated in recent days. The RFI has been referenced in reporting by outlets including Naval News, The Week, Marine Insight and idrw.

As described in that coverage, the requirement calls for a munition with a range of at least 1,000 km and a loiter endurance of nine hours or more. The same reporting says the weapon is to be canister-launched and fitted with a stabilised electro-optical/infrared seeker.

The document itself is not new. The intake note records the RFI as dating from mid-August, with the trade press recirculating it roughly two days ago. That gap matters for framing: this is a month-old procurement notice returning to circulation, not a fresh announcement.

An RFI is an early market-survey step rather than a purchase order or contract. Nothing in the material seen so far indicates how many units the ministry might eventually seek, what the budget could be, which service or command would field the system, or which vendors have responded. No official statement from the ministry has been seen on the wire.

Before this runs, the desk needs to obtain and read the RFI itself, including its issuing directorate, reference number, exact issue date and response deadline, and confirm the range, endurance, launch method and seeker specifications directly from that document rather than from secondary coverage. We also need a comment or confirmation from the Ministry of Defence, and a check on whether the RFI is still open or has since closed. Until the primary document is in hand, every specification in this brief should be treated as reported by trade outlets and not independently verified.

blocks.label: Headline
lines: रक्षा मंत्रालय ने 1,000 किलोमीटर मारक क्षमता वाले जहाज-प्रक्षेपित लॉइटरिंग म्यूनिशन की तलाश शुरू की: रिपोर्ट

blocks.label: Body
lines: हाल के दिनों में प्रसारित व्यापार-जगत की खबरों के अनुसार, भारत के रक्षा मंत्रालय ने एक मीडियम रेंज लॉइटरिंग म्यूनिशन के लिए सूचना हेतु अनुरोध (आरएफआई) जारी किया है, जिसे जहाजों और तट-आधारित वाहनों से समुद्री तथा जमीनी दोनों तरह के लक्ष्यों के विरुद्ध दागा जा सके। इस आरएफआई का उल्लेख नेवल न्यूज़, द वीक, मरीन इनसाइट और idrw समेत कई प्रकाशनों की रिपोर्टिंग में किया गया है।

इन खबरों में बताया गया है कि इस आवश्यकता के तहत हथियार की मारक क्षमता कम से कम 1,000 किलोमीटर और लॉइटर एंड्योरेंस नौ घंटे या उससे अधिक होनी चाहिए। इसी रिपोर्टिंग के मुताबिक, यह हथियार कनिस्टर से प्रक्षेपित किया जाने वाला होगा और इसमें स्थिरीकृत इलेक्ट्रो-ऑप्टिकल/इन्फ्रारेड सीकर लगा होगा।

दस्तावेज़ स्वयं नया नहीं है। इनटेक नोट के अनुसार यह आरएफआई अगस्त के मध्य का है, जिसे व्यापार-जगत के प्रकाशनों ने लगभग दो दिन पहले दोबारा प्रसारित किया। यह अंतर संदर्भ के लिहाज़ से मायने रखता है: यह एक महीने पुरानी खरीद सूचना का दोबारा चलन में आना है, न कि कोई ताज़ा घोषणा।

आरएफआई खरीद आदेश या अनुबंध नहीं, बल्कि बाज़ार सर्वेक्षण का एक शुरुआती चरण होता है। अब तक देखी गई सामग्री में ऐसा कुछ नहीं है जिससे पता चले कि मंत्रालय आगे चलकर कितनी इकाइयाँ लेना चाहेगा, बजट क्या हो सकता है, कौन-सी सेना या कमान इस प्रणाली को तैनात करेगी, या किन विक्रेताओं ने जवाब दिया है। वायर पर मंत्रालय का कोई आधिकारिक बयान नहीं देखा गया है।

इसे प्रकाशित करने से पहले डेस्क को आरएफआई स्वयं प्राप्त कर उसे पढ़ना होगा, जिसमें जारी करने वाला निदेशालय, संदर्भ संख्या, सटीक जारी तिथि और उत्तर देने की अंतिम तिथि शामिल है, तथा मारक क्षमता, एंड्योरेंस, प्रक्षेपण पद्धति और सीकर विशिष्टताओं की पुष्टि द्वितीयक खबरों के बजाय सीधे उसी दस्तावेज़ से करनी होगी। हमें रक्षा मंत्रालय से टिप्पणी या पुष्टि भी चाहिए, और यह जाँचना होगा कि आरएफआई अब भी खुला है या बंद हो चुका है। जब तक प्राथमिक दस्तावेज़ हाथ में नहीं आता, इस ब्रीफ में दी गई हर विशिष्टता को व्यापार प्रकाशनों द्वारा रिपोर्ट किया गया और स्वतंत्र रूप से असत्यापित ही माना जाना चाहिए।

brief.headline: MoD said to seek ship-launched loitering munition with 1,000-km range
brief.body:
India's Ministry of Defence has issued a Request for Information for a Medium Range Loitering Munition that could be fired from ships and from shore-based vehicles against both maritime and land targets, according to trade coverage circulated in recent days. The RFI has been referenced in reporting by outlets including Naval News, The Week, Marine Insight and idrw.

As described in that coverage, the requirement calls for a munition with a range of at least 1,000 km and a loiter endurance of nine hours or more. The same reporting says the weapon is to be canister-launched and fitted with a stabilised electro-optical/infrared seeker.

The document itself is not new. The intake note records the RFI as dating from mid-August, with the trade press recirculating it roughly two days ago. That gap matters for framing: this is a month-old procurement notice returning to circulation, not a fresh announcement.

An RFI is an early market-survey step rather than a purchase order or contract. Nothing in the material seen so far indicates how many units the ministry might eventually seek, what the budget could be, which service or command would field the system, or which vendors have responded. No official statement from the ministry has been seen on the wire.

Before this runs, the desk needs to obtain and read the RFI itself, including its issuing directorate, reference number, exact issue date and response deadline, and confirm the range, endurance, launch method and seeker specifications directly from that document rather than from secondary coverage. We also need a comment or confirmation from the Ministry of Defence, and a check on whether the RFI is still open or has since closed. Until the primary document is in hand, every specification in this brief should be treated as reported by trade outlets and not independently verified.
